Safe (0 to 12.0 ug/m3): Maintain Proper Tire Pressure: Keep vehicle tires inflated to minimize road dust and particulate friction.
Use Electric Lawn Equipment: Switch to battery-powered mowers and leaf blowers to prevent small-engine soot.
Keep Home Clean: Regularly vacuum with a HEPA filter vacuum to capture settled indoor dust particles.
Service Heating Systems: Inspect home furnaces annually to ensure clean and complete fuel combustion.
Choose Active Transit: Walk or bike for short trips to reduce tire and brake wear emissions.
Plant Dense Greenery: Grow thick hedges or trees near property lines to act as natural dust and particle filters.
Seal Windows and Doors: Prevent outdoor road dust and fine particles from drifting indoors.
Organize Street Sweeping Drives: Coordinate community campaigns to clear accumulated street soot and brake dust.
Support Controlled Burns Management: Participate in local forestry brush-clearing to prevent catastrophic wildfire smoke.
Establish Clean Construction Rules: Advocate for local building regulations requiring dust suppression on job sites.
Moderate (12.1 to 35.4 ug/m3): Upgrade HVAC Filters: Install MERV 11 or higher filters in home heating and cooling systems.
Avoid Wood Burning: Refrain from using indoor fireplaces or backyard fire pits during moderate haze days.
Combine Daily Errands: Group multiple driving trips into a single loop to reduce cold-start particulate exhaust.
Wipe Down Surfaces: Clean window sills and hard floors with damp cloths instead of dry sweeping.
Limit Dust-Heavy Chores: Postpone sweeping driveways or handling dry garden soil on calm, stagnant days.
Check Air Quality Monitors: Review local particulate forecasts before planning outdoor physical activities.
Drive Smoother: Avoid rapid acceleration and hard braking to minimize brake pad wear particles.
Promote Public Transit Challenges: Organize workplace or school carpooling initiatives to cut traffic volume.
Run Community Dust Alerts: Set up neighborhood networks to share warnings about local construction or smoke events.
Advocate for Paved Roads: Work with local authorities to pave or treat unpaved local roads prone to dust.
Dangerous (35.5+ ug/m3): Run HEPA Air Purifiers: Operate high-efficiency air purifiers continuously inside primary living areas.
Seal Home Openings: Keep all windows and doors tightly closed to block heavy smoke or particulate infiltration.
Wear N95 Respirators: Use a certified N95 or P100 mask if going outside during high particulate events.
Postpone Outdoor Exertion: Shift all physical exercise and heavy labor indoors to avoid deep lung inhalation.
Set Vehicle to Recirculate: Use cabin air recirculation when driving through heavy smoke or smog zones.
Avoid Indoor Combustion: Do not burn candles, incense, or use gas stoves without exhaust fans.
Stay Indoors: Limit non-essential outdoor movement until air particulate levels subside.
Set Up Community Clean Air Shelters: Open public indoor spaces equipped with industrial air filtration for residents.
Distribute Emergency Masks: Partner with local groups to provide N95 masks to vulnerable populations.
Coordinate Emergency Remote Work: Partner with employers and schools to trigger temporary work-from-home rules.
